The Indian women's team successfully defended its South Asian Football Federation(SAFF) Women's Championship title for the fifth time in a row with a 3-1 win over Nepal in March 2019 at the Sahid Rangashala Stadium in Biratnagar, Nepal. Dalima Chhibber opened the scoring for India in the first half, with Dangmei Grace and Anju Tamang finding the net in the second half after Sabitra Bhandari got the equaliser for Nepal in the first half. The win extends India's unbeaten run in the tournament's history to 23 games.

The Alai Darwaza was erected by Ala-ud-Din Khalji, a Sultan of Delhi (r.1296-1316) in c.1305 as the southern entrance gateway to the Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque. The mosque is the earliest surviving in India and stands in the Qutb complex. The Alai Darwaza is thought to have been one of four gateways planned along the walls and is the only one surviving.

Article 338B of the Indian Constitution states that there shall be a commission for the backward classes known as National Commission for Backward classes (NCBC) and it also contains the composition of the NCBC in it. The article defines the procedure of appointing the members of the commission and their duties to be performed by them.

The first batch of 100 women soldiers in the Army is likely to be commissioned by March 2021, Army sources said in September 2019. They said the commissioning will take place after the first batch completes its training, which will commence in December 2019. The women soldiers will be commissioned into the Corps of Military Police of the Indian Army.

Indus Waters Treaty, treaty, signed on September 19, 1960, between India and Pakistan and brokered by the World Bank. The treaty fixed and delimited the rights and obligations of both countries concerning the use of the waters of the Indus River system. The Indus is the western most River system in the subcontinent. Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas and Satluj are its main tributaries.

Ravindra Nath Tagore renounced his Knighthood in protest for Jalianwalla Bagh mass killing in 1919. The Jallianwala Bagh massacre, also known as the Amritsar massacre, took place on 13 April 1919. A large peaceful crowd had gathered at the Jalianwalla Bagh in Amritsar, Punjab, to protest against the Rowlatt Act and arrest of pro-independence activists Saifuddin Kitchlew and Satyapal.

The "Excavated remains of Nalanda Mahavihara", the great monastic-cum-scholastic establishment are located around 88 km away from Patna, state capital of Bihar in India. It presents a key archaeological evidence of a truly international centre for organised learning. Nalanda Mahavihara was founded by Kumargupta I of the Gupta dynasty in 5th century CE. It was patronized by various rulers including King Harshavardhana of Kannauj (7th century CE) and the Pala rulers (8th - 12th century CE) as well as various scholars.

Girish Chandra Murmu is the first Lieutenant Governor of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir. Murmu took oath as the lieutenant governor of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir in July 2020 as J-K officially lost its statehood and was spilt into two UTs- Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh.

The Ghadar Party was formed on 15 July 1913, and it was initially named as the Pacific Coast Hindustan Association. It was established in the United States under the leadership of Lala Har Dayal, Sant Baba Wasakha Singh Dadehar, Baba Jawala Singh, Santokh Singh and Sohan Singh Bhakna as its president.

The Padma Awards are one of the highest civilian honours of India announced annually on the eve of Republic Day. The Awards are given in three categories: Padma Vibhushan (for exceptional and distinguished service), Padma Bhushan (distinguished service of higher order) and Padma Shri (distinguished service). The award seeks to recognize achievements in all fields of activities or disciplines where an element of public service is involved.

The deletion, which is made from the value of gross investment in order to accommodate regular wear and tear of capital goods, is called depreciation. Depreciation does not take into account unexpected or sudden destruction or disuse of capital as can happen with accidents, natural calamities or other such extraneous circumstances.

The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) is the governing body for cricket in India. Its headquarters are situated at Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai. The board was formed in December 1928 as a society, registered under the Tamil Nadu Societies Registration Act.

The Kameng-Sonitpur Elephant Reserve (KSER) is located in the eastern hill forests of Arunachal Pradesh and Assam in India, and its area is about 7500 sq. km. This reserve is currently home to approximately 1200 elephants.

Arunima Sinha is the world's first female amputee to climb Mount Everest. On 21st May 2013, Arunima reached the summit of Everest as part of the Tata Group Sponsored Eco Everest Expedition, becoming the first female amputee to scale the famous mountain. In 2014, Arunima's book, 'Born Again on the Mountain' was published, the launch was attended by the Prime Minister of India, Narenda Modi.In 2015, she was awarded Padma Shri, the fourth highest civilian award in India. She is also the recipient of the Tenzing Norgay Highest Mountaineering Award in India.

Pancha Rathas is a monument complex at Mahabalipuram, on the Coromandel Coast of the Bay of Bengal, in the Kancheepuram district of the state of Tamil Nadu, India. Pancha Rathas is an example of monolithic Indian rock-cut architecture.

The structures are named after the Pancha Pandavas and their common wife Draupadi, of epic Mahabharata fame. In order of their size, they include the Dharmaraja Ratha, Bhima Ratha, Arjuna Ratha, Nakula Sahadeva Ratha, and Draupadi Ratha.

In 2019, the UK High Court today upheld the claims of India in the 70 years old ≤35 million fund that is being held by the National Westminster Bank in London. The Fund had been held in the account of the High Commissioner of Pakistan to the UK Rahimtoola since September 1948. It had been the subject of earlier proceedings in 1950s in which the UK House of Lords set aside proceedings brought by the 7th Nizam of Hyderabad claiming the Fund as Pakistan invoked state immunity.

'Capital - Hangzhou Grand Canal'("Grand Canal"), a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is the longest canal or artificial river in the world. The Grand Canal starts in Beijing and ends at the city of Hangzhou in Zhejiang province.

Pernicious anaemia is caused by Vitamin B12 deficiency. Pernicious anaemia is an autoimmune condition that affects your stomach. An autoimmune condition means your immune system, the body's natural defence system that protects against illness and infection, attacks your body's healthy cells.

questions.solution: Jaisalmer is also known as the 'Golden City'. Jaisalmer is the largest district of Rajasthan which is spread over 38,401 sq. km. Jaisalmer is enveloped with a golden hue tint overlooking the city thereby earning the title of the Golden City of India.

The aggregate value of goods and services produced in an economy can be calculated by three methods: income method, expenditure method and value added/product method.

The production approach sums the "value-added" at each stage of production, where value-added is defined as total sales less the value of intermediate inputs into the production process.

Unsaturated hydrocarbons add hydrogen in the presence of catalysts such as palladium or nickel to give saturated hydrocarbons. Catalysts are substances that cause a reaction to occur or proceed at a different rate without the reaction itself being affected. This reaction is commonly used in the hydrogenation of vegetable oils using a nickel catalyst. Vegetable oils generally have long unsaturated carbon chains while animal fats have saturated carbon chains.

questions.questionHtml:
If 5cosθ - 12sinθ = 0, then what is the value of
1 + sinθ + cosθ_________1 - sinθ + cosθ
? 

यदि 5cosθ - 12sinθ = 0 है, तो
1 + sinθ + cosθ_________1 - sinθ + cosθ
1 + sinθ + cosθ/1 - sinθ + cosθ

का मान कितना है?
questions.solution:
Given,

5 cosθ - 12 sin θ = 0

5 cos θ = 12 sinθ

sinθ/cosθ = 5/12

tanθ = 5/12 = perpendicular/base

By Pythagoras theorem,

Hypotenuse = √ {(base2) + (perpendicular)2}

Hypotenuse = √ (144 + 25) = √169

Hypotenuse = 13 unit

sinθ = Perpendicular/Hypotenuse = 5/13 and cos θ = Base/Hypotenuse = 12/13

Now,

(1 + sinθ + cos θ)/(1 - sinθ + cosθ)

= (1 + 5/13 + 12/13)/(1 - 5/13 + 12/13)

= (13 + 12 + 5)/(13 - 5 + 12)

= 30/20

= 3/2

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. They are constructing a residential youth hostel.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

They are constructing a residential youth hostel.

options.text: A residential youth hostel is constructed by them
options.html: A residential youth hostel is constructed by them

options.text: A residential youth hostel was constructed by them.
options.html: A residential youth hostel was constructed by them.

options.text: A residential youth hostel has been constructed by them
options.html: A residential youth hostel has been constructed by them

options.text: A residential youth hostel is being constructed by them
options.html: A residential youth hostel is being constructed by them

questions.solution:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive Voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Present Continuous. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Present Continuous.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + am/is/are + V1 + ing + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + am/is/are + being + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

Arnab is typing a document. (Active Voice)

A document is being typed by Arnab. (Passive Voice)

The options except (d) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: option (d).

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech. "Hello", he said to his friend. "What can I do for you?""

questions.solution:
In the case of Interrogative sentences like this, "said" in Direct Speech is changed into "enquired (of)", "wanted to know", "asked", etc.

In Indirect speech, the verb is always placed after the subject, unlike in Direct Speech.

For example:

The teacher said to him, "What is your name?" (Direct Speech)

The teacher asked him what his name was. (Indirect Speech)

Also, the sentence in the Direct Speech is in the present indefinite tense. So, the tense in the Indirect Speech should be in the past indefinite tense.

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

· Modal verb 'can' will change to 'could'.

· 'Said to' will be transformed to 'greeted', as 'hello' is mentioned in the sentence.

· The pronoun 'I' will change to 'he' as per the subject and 'you' will change to 'him' as per the object.

Therefore, the correct answer is: option (c).

questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. Although I had a fear of water, I thought it was an important skill I should learn. B. However, what I didn't realize was that it would also make me a more confident person. C. I also thought it would be a good exercise that would make me physically stronger. D. One of the hardest things I've had to do was to learn how to swim.
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Although I had a fear of water, I thought it was an important skill I should learn.

B. However, what I didn't realize was that it would also make me a more confident person.

C. I also thought it would be a good exercise that would make me physically stronger.

D. One of the hardest things I've had to do was to learn how to swim.
questions.solution:
After reading all the sentences, we can see that 'D' is the first sentence as it introduces the activity in which the author is indulged (swimming) and the whole paragraph revolves around the topic of swimming. 'D-A' is the mandatory pair as it is mentioned in 'D' that it is the hardest thing for him, but still he chose to learn it, will be the next sentence. What are various influences that the person feels, is mentioned in the latter part of the sentence. 'C' is the third sentence of the paragraph as it suggests that the person thought of getting a good physical strength, additionally what he/she got is mentioned in sentence 'B' which makes it the last part of the paragraph.

The correct order of rearrangement is DACB.

Hence, option (c) is correct.
